title: Applied ML experiment scratchpad - 2026-03-28
content:
Morning notes / plan:
- Quick local runs to reproduce weird degenerate outputs from last night (q4f on redwood-v2-small).
- Evaluate prompt set A (20 instruction-style QA prompts) + few-shot clarifying turns.
- Check KV cache correctness when switching quantized model mid-rollout.
- Log perf (tokens/s), p50/p95 latency, and sample quality (manual inspect + simple heuristics).

Context / background:
- Yesterday saw occasional hallucinations on long context (>1k tokens) when using q4f quantized weights on redwood-v2-small. Suspect subtle rounding causing attention score drift when past key/value cache gets reused across batches. Only reproduced intermittently.
- Baseline (fp16) consistently fine. q8_0 seemed stable but slower with larger memory footprint on our infra.

Experiments run (2026-03-28):
1) run-id: ml-scratch-20260328-01
   model: redwood-v2-small (fp16)
   quant: none
   prompt: prompt-set-A (instructions + 3-shot)
   temp: 0.2, top_p: 0.95, seed: 42
   seq_len: 1024
   notes: baseline, no cache reuse across batches.
   metrics: approx 145 tok/s, p50 18ms, p95 76ms. quality: good (no hallucinations on the 20 QA prompts).

2) run-id: ml-scratch-20260328-02
   model: redwood-v2-small
   quant: q4f (per-channel asymmetric + small-scale calibration)
   prompt: prompt-set-A (same)
   temp: 0.2, seed: 42
   seq_len: 1024
   notes: enabled KV cache reuse, batching size=8
   metrics: approx 315 tok/s (local GPU), p50 26ms, p95 110ms. observed 2/20 prompts with short hallucinations (extra fabricated detail).
   hypothesis: small negative bias introduced in attention logits during quantized matmul when accumulating cached KV across multiple batches. Might be numerical drift in softmax tails.

3) run-id: ml-scratch-20260328-03
   model: redwood-v2-small
   quant: q8_0
   prompt: prompt-set-A
   notes: q8_0 stable, fewer hallucinations (0/20), but memory backpressure caused oom on one host under burst.
   metrics: approx 260 tok/s, p50 29ms, p95 125ms.

Quick digging notes:
- Reproduced the q4f issue by toggling cache reuse: reproduce when cache reused across >=3 segments. If we clear cache between segments, issue disappears.
- Tried deterministic seed & CPU-side softmax compare: small differences (<1e-3) in logits accumulate for long sequences. Float32 accumulation appears to avoid drift.
- Kernel investigation: q4f path uses fused int8 GEMM + dequantize to float16 -> matmul -> fused add. Might be precision loss rounding in the dequantize step.

Prompt set A (summary):
- 20 short instruction prompts covering: fact recall, reasoning 2-step, commonsense, and one adversarial ambiguous prompt.
- Few-shot examples chosen to bias toward concise answers.

Immediate actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Run ablation: q4f with FP32 accumulation flag (if runtime supports) to see if accumulation precision fixes it. (priority: high)
- [ ] Add log hook to capture pre-softmax logits for failing examples (to diff vs fp16 baseline). (priority: high)
- [ ] Try per-layer higher precision for attention logits only (keep rest q4f) to narrow root cause. (priority: medium)
- [ ] Run longer context (>2k) tests to check scaling of divergence. (priority: low)
- [ ] Slack Asha & Jordan with summary + attach minimal repro snippet.

Notes for repro snippet to share:
- Minimal loop: load q4f weights -> run autoregressive generation with cache reuse across 4 segments -> compare final token logits vs fp16 run. Save seeds + prompts.
- Capture env: CUDA driver, pytorch 2.1rc, triton kernels version.

Hypotheses (short):
- H1: quantization dequant/accum rounding in fused kernel causes small bias that propagates via softmax over long contexts and leads to occasional hallucination.
- H2: batching + cache reuse interacts with scheduling leading to stale KV indexes (less likely given checksums matched).
- H3: calibration scale mismatch for some layers (rare outliers) -> correctable with per-channel recalibration.

Logs / snippets (copied here for quick reference):
- failing prompt example (trimmed): "When did the company open its first EU office?" -> fp16: "We opened our first EU office in 2019 in Berlin." q4f: "We opened our first EU office in 2019 in Paris, near the Rhine." (fabricated 'near the Rhine' detail)

- rough command used: 
  python -m serve.eval_runner --model redwood-v2-small --quant q4f --prompts prompts/a_set.json --batch 8 --seed 42 --cache-reuse true --log-pre-softmax logs/q4f-run-01.json

Ideas for mitigation in-prod:
- For customers on dedicated/private that need low-latency with quantization enabled, fall back to q8_0 for long-context routes until we pin the bug.
- Add probabilistic sanity-check for top-k overlap with fp16 baseline on small sample of requests (can be offline sampling route).

Next steps (today):
- Run ablation with FP32 accumulation & per-layer higher precision for attention (estimate ~2-3 hrs).
- Prepare short summary Slack to Asha/Jordan + attach failing prompt / minimal repro.
- If repro is consistent, open JIRA and assign to infra-kernels with logs and small repro.

Random notes / brain dump:
- We should add an internal test in the rollout pipeline that runs a 100-example long-context probe whenever a quantized model is promoted. Catch these regressions early.
- Consider swapping to stochastic quantization for attention layers as an experiment (might reduce systematic bias).

End of scratchpad.
